The AI Agent gold rush is here — but most builders are drowning in tool choices.

Forget 50-tool stacks. Here’s the minimal setup for powers production agents:

1️⃣ Design – Miro to map logic before building
2️⃣ Framework – LangGraph for orchestration or Phidata for fast production
3️⃣ Data Layer – Supabase for storage and auth
4️⃣ Memory – Zep or LangMem for adaptive context
5️⃣ Testing – LangSmith for debugging

That’s it. 5 tools. Build real agents, not tech clutter.

While everyone else is chasing distractions, I’m chasing knowledge. ⚡

Everyone’s building AI agents

Almost no one knows which orchestration framework to use 

Here’s how to stop winging it :

⭕️ Use n8n when:

 • You’re integrating LLMs with tools
 • Your flow is trigger → AI → action
 • You want fast, no-code deployment
 • You don’t need agent memory

 ⭕️ Use LangGraph when:

 • Your agents need to think, loop, reflect
 • You want memory + state across steps
 • You’re building logic trees, retries, branching 
  paths
 • You need observability
My first successful automation on n8n.

In a study of 107 male Y Combinator founders, a surprising correlation between age-normalized testosterone and company stage was uncovered. Testosterone, a hormone associated with confidence, dominance, and drive, increased by 55.7% from pre-seed to seed funding, peaking at the Series B stage, where levels were 99.6% higher than pre-seed. After series B funding, testosterone was observed to drop by 42.2%, coinciding with a spike in cortisol levels.

"Do things that don't scale."

This is originally from an essay by Paul Graham, the Founder of Y Combinator.

And Brian Chesky of Airbnb famously took this approach.

Early on, when Airbnb had no listings, he and his co-founders went around New York City taking photos of the apartments and helping hosts improve their listings because the hosts didn’t know how to market their listings.

As a founder myself...

This is an idea I think about often while running my business. ↓
